title: Room Reservations Booking Conditions: One Room per Reservation
content:
**Clause.** Under Room Reservations a guest profile may hold any number of reservations at any number of hotels at the same time; there is no brand-wide cap on reservations per guest. Reservations at the same hotel for overlapping nights are limited separately, by the rooms-per-stay limit of the rate plans involved. Each reservation covers exactly one room and is cancelled, changed, checked in and charged on its own; a request about one confirmation number never changes another reservation.

## What the clause means in practice

| Matter | Position |
|---|---|
| Reservations one guest may hold across the brand | No cap |
| Rooms one reservation covers | Exactly one |
| Reservations at the same hotel for overlapping nights | Limited separately by the rooms-per-stay limit |
| Effect of a request made under one confirmation number | Confined to that reservation |

## Points of judgement

**A guest holds reservations at three different Ashbury hotels for the same week. Is any of them affected by the others?** No. There is no brand-wide cap on reservations per guest, and reservations at different hotels are not counted together.

**A guest asks to cancel the reservation behind one confirmation number and also holds a second room at that hotel for the same nights. What does the cancellation touch?** Only the reservation behind the confirmation number named. Each reservation is cancelled, changed, checked in and charged on its own, and a request about one confirmation number never changes another reservation.

**A family needs two rooms. How is that booked?** As two reservations, because each reservation covers exactly one room; each then carries its own confirmation number, guarantee and charges.
